title: Best object detection models for NVIDIA A100 (2026)
dek: On an NVIDIA A100 under PyTorch FP32, D-FINE-X leads accuracy at 59.3 mAP while RT-DETR-R34 runs fastest at 27.8 FPS. Pick by accuracy, not latency.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: D-FINE-X leads accuracy on the NVIDIA A100 at 59.3 mAP@50-95, running 15.4 FPS under PyTorch FP32. The fastest measured model is RT-DETR-R34 at 27.8 FPS and 48.2 mAP. Every model here runs in well under 100 ms per image on this card, so latency rarely decides the pick: choose by accuracy. mAP is shown here in percent form.

The A100 has enough headroom that even the largest detector in this set clears 15 FPS. That changes how you read the leaderboard: on edge hardware the accuracy leaders are often unusable, but here the top of the table is a real deployment option. Read the accuracy table first, then use the speed table only if you are batching high volumes.

blocks.caption: Top detectors by COCO val2017 mAP@50-95 on NVIDIA A100 (PyTorch FP32).

blocks.text: Six models hold the measured frontier: RT-DETR-R34, RT-DETR-R50m, RT-DETR-R50, D-FINE-M, D-FINE-L, and D-FINE-X. It runs from D-FINE-X at 59.3 mAP down to RT-DETR-R34 at 48.2 mAP and 27.8 FPS. Anything off this list is beaten on both accuracy and speed by a model on it. The three YOLO-NAS entries all fall behind a D-FINE or RT-DETR model at similar cost.

blocks.caption: Fastest detectors on NVIDIA A100 (PyTorch FP32), by throughput.

blocks.text: Every model in this set finishes under 100 ms per image, so a 100 ms budget buys the full accuracy leader: D-FINE-X at 59.3 mAP and 64.71 ms. If you need the highest sustained throughput instead, RT-DETR-R34 clears 27.8 FPS at 48.2 mAP. The mid-frontier D-FINE-L holds 57.2 mAP at 17.1 FPS, and D-FINE-M holds 55.1 mAP at 21.7 FPS. On this card the choice is which accuracy tier you want, not what will run in time.
